purpose: Reconcile two citation conventions that name one Sanskrit word, so that a convention difference is not reported as a graph defect.
why_this_file_exists: A first scoring pass reported 196 Rigvedic deity mentions as refuted. Nearly all of them were this: our registry prints the deity of the waters as 'apah' and the Treebank of Vedic Sanskrit prints its lemma as 'ap'. Same word, two conventions, and no string rule separates that case from a real wrong-word match without also merging words that differ. So the reconciliation is written down, entry by entry, with the human token count beside it, and a reader who disagrees with an entry can strike it and re-run.
not_gold: This is a bridge between two naming conventions, not an annotation of any Vedic text, and not a judgement on any graph claim. Every graph claim in this artifact is decided by the human treebank, never by this file. This file only decides whether two labels are the same word.
scope_limit: Only paradigms where the two forms are standard allomorphs of one stem in any Vedic grammar. Where the two are different words that the registry chose to group, no entry is made and the pair is reported as REGISTRY_SYNONYM_EXPANSION instead.

allomorphs.grounds: ap- is the treebank citation of the same defective plural stem our registry cites as apah (nom.pl. apah / acc. apas / loc. apsu). One paradigm.
Same stem as the concept; the graph's own Zurich evidence cites this deity's lemma as ap-, which agrees.
dyaus / div- is the textbook heteroclite paradigm: nom. dyauh, gen. divah. One word.
ahan- / ahar- is the standard r/n heteroclite alternation of one neuter stem.
Our label is the nominative plural of the stem the treebank cites as pitr-. One paradigm.
As above; the Zurich evidence for this deity also cites pitar-.
sakhya- is the abstract derived from sakhi-. Treated as one word here because the registry's own alias list mixes the two (sakhye, sakha), so the layer is not distinguishing them either.
havis- and havya- are both the -is/-ya derivatives of hu- 'pour', and every printed lexicon glosses both as the oblation itself.

virya- is the abstract of vira-. Kept as one entry rather than two because the registry lists viryam under VIRA-HERO deliberately; flagged in the report as a hero/heroism conflation the layer does not separate.
Same jan- paradigm family; janiman- appears in the treebank as a variant of janman- itself.
REJECTED AS AN ALLOMORPH. prthivi and bhumi are different words. Recorded here only so the decision is visible; scored as a registry synonym.

REJECTED AS AN ALLOMORPH. vata and vayu are distinct Vedic words and the graph carries VG:DEVATA:VAYUH separately, so folding vayu- into the concept 'wind' crosses an identity the graph itself maintains. Reported as a probable registry defect, not a bridge entry.

rejected_entries_are_not_bridges: The last two entries carry grounds beginning REJECTED and are NOT applied as bridges by the scorer. They are recorded because a reader must be able to see what was considered and refused, not only what was accepted.
